title: Signal digest: quantization onboarding & eval roadmap (Feb 14 2027)
content:
Purpose:
A compact weeknote capturing the current state of quantization experiments, onboarding checklist for two candidate models, and a prioritized eval roadmap. Intended for the weekly applied-ml sync and to hand off to solutions engineering for early customer trials.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Continued q4_k_m experiments on Llama-2-13B and Mosaic-7B. Best perf tradeoff so far: q4_k_m + symmetric per-channel rounding with small activation calibration gives ~1.8x token throughput vs float and <3% relative drop on downstream chat-turn accuracy in our in-house eval set.
- Onboarding: Mosaic-7B pipeline mostly green (KV cache tweaks + custom attention kernel). Llama-2-13B shows KV-cache memory spike in long-context scenarios — probable root cause is our current KV packing layout.
- Evals: Started targeted reranker/regression evals (100 short dialogs, 300 instructions). Need larger evals (1k+) before can propose promoting quant config to staging.

Standup highlights (Feb 10–14):
- Mon: Ran burst experiment with mixed-precision (attn kernels FP16, matmuls INT4 packed) — infra logs show fewer CUDA memory allocations but increased kernel time for final matmul in 8/64 micro-batches. Notebook: INF-quant/burst-0210.ipynb (WIP).
- Tue: Ethan repro'd KV-cache spike for Llama-2-13B using long-context generator tests (~8k tokens). Reproduced locally on a single A100-80GB.
- Wed: Marta pushed the KV packing patch (PR#981) to serving-runtime; initial performance regression fixed in local perf harness.
- Thu: Small-scale human eval on chat-turn coherence (n=120); q4_k_m config scored 91/120 vs fp16 baseline 94/120. Notable failure modes: hallucinated entities in narratives, slightly shorter generated outputs.
- Fri: Retro + planning — decided to expand evals to include fallback tests (if quality regresses, auto-fallback to fp16 for first n tokens).

Experiment snapshot (most recent runs):
- Models: Llama-2-13B, Mosaic-7B.
- Configs tested: fp16-baseline, q4_k_m symmetric-per-channel (calib 512 steps), q4_k_m asymmetric per-tensor, q8_0 mixed.
- Throughput (tokens/s) on 1xA100-80GB, batch size 4, seq_len 512:
  - fp16: 320 tok/s
  - q4_k_m (sym pc, calib512): 590 tok/s
  - q4_k_m (asym): 570 tok/s
  - q8_0 mixed: 410 tok/s
- Downstream evals (relative to fp16 baseline):
  - Perplexity (wikitext-sample, 5k tokens): fp16=1.00 (ref), q4_k_m=1.06, q8_0=1.02.
  - Reranker accuracy (internal dev set, 300 queries): fp16=0.88, q4_k_m=0.85 (drop -3.4%), q8_0=0.87.
  - Chat-turn coherence (human n=120): fp16=94/120, q4_k_m=91/120.

Observations and interpretation:
- q4_k_m offers substantial throughput gains; quality degradation is modest but non-uniform across tasks. Reranking and instruction-following are more sensitive than plain next-token prediction.
- Activation calibration (512 steps) improved q4_k_m stability vs naive symmetric quantization; recommend keeping calibration step in onboarding.
- KV-cache memory anomaly appears tied to our packing order when seq_len > 4096; likely an indexing bug in the packing function rather than model artifact.

Blockers / Risks:
- Long-context KV memory regression for Llama-2-13B blocks promotion to Dedicated early-access for customers needing >4k context.
- Human eval capacity: we need 1k+ turns for statistically confident quality deltas; current budget only covers ~300.
- Regression monitoring: no automated rollout gate exists to compare prompt-level outputs live for KPIs (cost/latency/QA).

Decisions made this week:
- Keep q4_k_m (sym PC + calib512) as the default candidate for staging for Mosaic-7B but hold off Llama-2-13B until KV issue fixed.
- Add an automatic fallback policy in runtime: if a response generation pass triggers "high-entity-hallucination" heuristics (heuristic flag), re-run first N tokens in fp16 for safety. Implementation tracked in INF-3421.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Ethan: finish KV-packing bugtrace and propose a minimal fix (PR) by 2027-02-18. (Owner: Ethan Zhou)
- Priya: expand reranker eval harness to 1k queries and schedule human eval ramp; coordinate with GTM for budget approval by 2027-02-21. (Owner: Priya N.)
- Marta: harden activation calibration flow; add calibration artifact uploader to model onboarding pipeline (contrib to model registry). ETA 2027-02-20.
- Leo: add rollout gate prototype in Console with a simple metric comparison panel (latency & quality delta) by next sync (2027-02-24).

Onboarding checklist status (candidate models):
- Mosaic-7B:
  - Model artifact pulled: done
  - Quant config validated (q4_k_m): done
  - KV-cache tests: passed (seq <= 4096)
  - Perf benchmark: passes internal SLOs -> READY for staging promo
- Llama-2-13B:
  - Model artifact pulled: done
  - Quant config validated: partial (fail on long-context)
  - KV-cache tests: fail on seq > 4096 -> HOLD
  - Perf benchmark: good for seq <= 4096

Next-week plan (prioritized):
1) Fix KV packing for Llama-2-13B and re-run long-context memory tests (blocking).
2) Run expanded reranker evals (1k) and collect human evals (1k turns).
3) Implement fallback-first-tokens prototype in runtime and simulate rollouts against historical traffic.
4) Draft a short one-pager for Solutions Eng: recommended quant settings per model class + observed tradeoffs for customer-facing docs.

Quick links / references:
- Jira: INF-3421 (fallback rollout prototype), INF-3499 (kv-cache packing), INF-3501 (evaluation expansion)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/981 (KV-packing draft)
- Notebook (WIP): internal://notebooks/INF-quant/burst-0210.ipynb
- Confluence: quant-patterns-2027 (draft)

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we instrument generation length and hallucination heuristic for each token window to get a better signal for when to fallback? (low-effort sensor)
- Consider running a latency-ablation to see where kernel time increases for mixed kernels; could guide micro-optimizations in the runtime kernel scheduler.

Recorded at: 2027-02-14 (initial) — edits: 2027-02-16 (added EK action items, updated metrics).
